prompt:
Feature: customize the AI prompts per group, from within Mealie.

Today the only way to change the prompts Mealie sends to AI providers is the OPENAI_CUSTOM_PROMPT_DIR setting: a folder of text files on the server that replace the built-in prompts for every group at once. Group managers cannot see or change prompts in the app, cannot add a preference such as "use metric units" without rewriting a whole prompt (and then missing later improvements to it), and admins cannot tune one group differently from another. We want prompt customization in the app, stored per group in the database, with the old folder imported once on upgrade.

Expected:

Backend

1. Built-in prompts (OpenAIService).
   - Prompts keep their dot-notation names and are read from text files under OpenAIService.PROMPTS_DIR as today ("category.name" is <category>/<name>.txt there), always through OpenAIService.PROMPTS_DIR at call time (tests monkeypatch it to a temporary folder). Prompts in the "system" category are system prompts: they transcribe the user's source faithfully instead of producing recipe data. Two prompts move into it: recipes.compile-source becomes system.compile-source and general.transcribe-audio becomes system.transcribe-audio (same text; everything that used the old names uses the new ones).
   - The debug prompt stops being a prompt (not listed, not customizable). OpenAIService.ping(provider, message, images=None) still calls get_response(prompt, message, response_schema=OpenAIText, attachments=images, provider=provider) and returns its result, but its prompt is now exactly the text of the file debug.txt in OpenAIService.TESTING_DIR (the same text as today's debug prompt); it must not depend on PROMPTS_DIR.
   - The built-in set is then recipes.build-recipe, recipes.parse-recipe-ingredients, recipes.parse-recipe-video, recipes.resolve-organizers, recipes.translate-recipe, system.compile-source and system.transcribe-audio.
   - New methods, callable on the class itself: get_prompt_names() gives every built-in prompt name found under PROMPTS_DIR, non-system prompts first, then system prompts. get_default_prompt(name) gives a built-in prompt's text, ignoring any customization, and raises OSError with "Unable to load prompt" in its message when the file can't be read (get_prompt keeps raising that too). _hash_prompt(content), a static method, gives a deterministic digest string of a prompt text (a hex SHA-256 works); it records which version of a built-in prompt an override was written against.
   - A module-level constant GLOBAL_PROMPT_NAME, whose value is "global", in the module that defines OpenAIService and OpenAIDataInjection (it is imported from that module, not from the package that re-exports OpenAIService). It is the reserved name of the group-wide instructions.
   - OPENAI_CUSTOM_PROMPT_DIR is retired: prompts are no longer read from that folder at runtime (the migration in item 5 imports its files), and OpenAIService no longer has a custom_prompt_dir attribute.

2. Stored customizations.
   - In the schema module that holds AIProviderCreate and AIProviderSettingsUpdate: AIPromptMode, a string enum with the members append and override (values "append" and "override"); AIPromptOverrideCreate with name, mode (AIPromptMode), content, and base_prompt_hash (optional, default None); and AIPromptOverrideOut with the same fields plus id, read from the ORM object and also built directly as AIPromptOverrideOut(id=..., name=..., mode=..., content=...). Content must contain something other than whitespace (blank content is a validation error) and is at most 20,000 characters.
   - A new table ai_prompt_overrides: id, settings_id (references ai_provider_settings.id, required), name, mode and content (required), base_prompt_hash (nullable), plus the usual created/updated timestamps; at most one row per prompt name per settings row. A group's customizations hang off its AI provider settings and go away with them when the group is deleted.
   - AllRepositories gets group_ai_prompt_overrides, a group-scoped repository: get_all() returns only that group's customizations (AIPromptOverrideOut objects), create(AIPromptOverrideCreate(...)) fills in the group's AI provider settings id by itself, and update and delete work by id as in the other repositories.
   - The group-wide instructions are stored the same way, as a customization named GLOBAL_PROMPT_NAME in append mode, with no hash.

3. OpenAIService.get_prompt(name, data_injections=None) applies the group's customizations.
   - It gets them from self.repos.group_ai_prompt_overrides.get_all(); unit tests hand overrides in through exactly that call on a mocked repos. When self.repos.group_id is falsy (unscoped repositories), nothing is applied and get_all() is not called at all.
   - Tests replace OpenAIService.__init__ with one that sets only self.repos (some also set default_provider, audio_provider and image_provider) and then use get_prompt and get_response. These must not need any other attribute set by __init__.
   - Not customized: exactly the built-in text.
   - Override: the override content replaces the built-in text. With nothing appended, get_prompt returns exactly the override content.
   - Appended instructions come after the base text (built-in or override). The result starts with the base text and a newline, then a short heading saying that what follows are additional instructions which take priority over conflicting instructions above (the result contains the words "take priority"), then the instructions, at the very end after a newline.
   - The group-wide instructions are appended to every non-system prompt, overridden ones included, before that prompt's own appended instructions; the two are separated by one blank line, so with group-wide "G" and own "P" the prompt ends with "G\n\nP". An overridden prompt with only group-wide "G" starts with "<override text>\n", ends with "\nG" and does not contain the built-in text.
   - System prompts take their own append or override, but never the group-wide instructions.
   - A customization of another prompt has no effect.
   - Data injections are still added after all of this, as today: in the result, the override comes before the group-wide instructions, which come before the injection's description, which comes before its value.

4. API. On success every prompt route answers 200 with the group's prompts, in camelCase: {"globalInstructions": text or null, "prompts": [{"name", "isSystem", "defaultContent", "mode", "content", "defaultChanged"}]}, with every key always present.
   - prompts has one entry per built-in prompt (the names of get_prompt_names(); "global" is not among them), non-system prompts first. isSystem is true for system prompts. defaultContent equals get_default_prompt(name). mode and content are null when the prompt isn't customized, otherwise the stored mode ("append" or "override") and content. defaultChanged is false unless the prompt is overridden and the hash stored with the override is set and differs from _hash_prompt of the current built-in text (for example a stored "stale"). Appended instructions are never flagged, and an override just saved through the API is not flagged.
   - For the current user's group, all three requiring can_manage (403 without it):
     - GET /api/groups/ai-providers/prompts
     - PUT /api/groups/ai-providers/prompts/{prompt_name} with {"mode": "append" or "override", "content": "..."}: creates or replaces the group's one customization of that prompt, storing the hash of the current built-in text. A PUT of append "first" and then override "second" leaves a single stored customization, with content "second" and mode override. prompt_name "global" sets the group-wide instructions, returned as globalInstructions; for "global" only append is allowed, and override answers 400. Blank content ("   ") answers 422.
     - DELETE /api/groups/ai-providers/prompts/{prompt_name}: removes the customization, so the prompt's mode and content are null again (globalInstructions is null for "global") and the repository holds nothing for it. Deleting a prompt that isn't customized also answers 200.
     - Any other prompt_name (for example "recipes.does-not-exist", "debug", "..secrets" or "recipes.nope") answers 404, for PUT and for DELETE.
   - The same three routes for admins, for any group: GET /api/admin/groups/{group_id}/ai-providers/prompts, and PUT and DELETE /api/admin/groups/{group_id}/ai-providers/prompts/{prompt_name}, with the same body, responses and 404. A non-admin gets 403 on all three. What an admin saves applies to that group: OpenAIService built with that group's repositories returns it from get_prompt.
   - Customizations are per group: another group's repository returns none of them, and its get_prompt still returns the built-in text.

5. A new Alembic migration: revision id a91720b8a7e7, revising the current head 1e69ea7cd45e, message "add ai prompt overrides", created 2026-10-15 20:11:05. Its file is named from these by the project's migration file template, so the name contains a91720b8a7e7 and sorts after the 1e69ea7cd45e file; the revisions stay one chain in file-name order. Its upgrade creates ai_prompt_overrides, then imports the legacy prompt folder:
   - The upgrade only uses alembic's op on the bound connection. It must work on a bare SQLite database that has nothing but an ai_provider_settings table (id CHAR(32)), run under Operations.context(MigrationContext.configure(connection)), with the module loaded on its own from its file path.
   - It reads OPENAI_CUSTOM_PROMPT_DIR when the upgrade runs, the way the old setting was read (environment variable, .env file, secrets directory), not from cached app settings. Unset, or not a directory: only the table is created.
   - Otherwise each legacy file that exists and is not blank becomes one row per row of ai_provider_settings: settings_id exactly as stored there, mode "override", content the file text unchanged, a new GUID id, and base_prompt_hash equal to OpenAIService._hash_prompt(OpenAIService.get_default_prompt(name)), so an imported override isn't flagged right away.
   - Files, relative to that folder, and the prompt names they become: recipes/build-recipe.txt, recipes/parse-recipe-ingredients.txt, recipes/parse-recipe-video.txt, recipes/resolve-organizers.txt and recipes/translate-recipe.txt keep their names (recipes.build-recipe and so on); recipes/compile-source.txt becomes system.compile-source; general/transcribe-audio.txt becomes system.transcribe-audio. Blank files (they used to fall back to the default), general/debug.txt and any other file (for example recipes/scrape-recipe.txt, a removed prompt) are skipped.
   - Downgrade drops the table.

6. Everything the AI provider API already does keeps working: provider CRUD (unknown id 404; the API key is write-only and never appears in create, get, update or settings responses nor in /api/groups/self; an update without apiKey keeps the stored key, one with it replaces it); settings (defaultProviderId, audioProviderId, imageProviderId and the providers list; deleting a provider clears the roles that used it); can_manage required (403) on providers, settings and connection tests; the connection tests at /api/groups/ai-providers/providers/test and /api/groups/ai-providers/providers/{provider_id}/test (tests patch OpenAIService.ping); empty settings for new groups, registered or admin-created; the admin provider routes for any group, and deleting a group; OpenAIService.test_connection and get_response as they behave today; and the AI ingredient parser.

Frontend

7. A new composable useAIPrompts(groupId?), exported from the composables module that holds useAIProviders (the spec mocks that module). It returns { prompts, loading, refresh, save, reset }: prompts is a ref holding the prompts response or null, loading a boolean ref, and refresh(), save(name, { mode, content }) and reset(name) call the GET, PUT and DELETE routes above (the admin routes for groupId when one is given), update prompts on success, and resolve to the new response, or to null when the request failed. Add the API client methods and the matching generated types (the spec imports the type AIPromptsOut from the group API types, the module with AIProviderOut).

8. A new component GroupAIPromptEditor, in the same folder as the spec (the spec imports it from there), with an optional groupId prop for admins. Show it on the group settings page and on the admin's group page; that wiring and the texts are not graded. The spec mounts it without Vuetify or Nuxt: only vue, @vueuse/core and vue-i18n are auto-imported, the en-US messages are loaded, $globals.icons is available in templates (icons.alert), useNuxtApp is stubbed, and the components named below are stubbed as plain elements.
   - Its data comes from useAIPrompts(). The editor builds its state from the composable's prompts ref, which is already filled when it mounts (the spec's refresh() resolves to null). Toasts, if any, use alert.success and alert.error from ~/composables/use-toast (mocked with only alert).
   - In DOM order: first the group-wide instructions editor (a v-textarea with v-model) and its save button, then one section per prompt, built from v-expansion-panels, v-expansion-panel, v-expansion-panel-title and v-expansion-panel-text with the content in their default slots (the stubs render only that, without the panel being opened). Each prompt section has a mode toggle, a v-btn-toggle bound to the mode whose v-btn children have the values "default", "append" and "override"; at most one editable v-textarea (v-model), for the current mode (none in default mode; the built-in text may be shown with the readonly prop); and its own save button, shown in every mode. The group-wide instructions have no mode toggle. Save buttons are BaseButton with the save prop, and no other button has that prop, so the first one is the group-wide one and the second belongs to the first prompt. A save button may be disabled when there is nothing to save, but never while its section differs from what is saved.
   - A prompt opens in its saved mode with its saved content (default when it isn't customized). The append and override editors keep their own text while the user switches modes. Switching to override fills an empty override editor with defaultContent, but keeps existing override text (an override "My prompt", switched to append and back to override, still shows "My prompt").
   - Saving a prompt in append or override mode calls save(name, { mode, content }) with that editor's text (append sends only the extra instructions, not the built-in text). Saving in default mode calls reset(name) and not save. Saving the group-wide instructions calls save("global", { mode: "append", content }) with the text trimmed, or reset("global") when it is empty. When save resolves to null, the user's mode and text stay as they were.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests tests/integration_tests/user_group_tests tests/integration_tests/admin_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

Frontend: `cd frontend && pnpm test:ci app/components/Domain/Group/GroupAIPromptEditor.test.ts`.
